5-0-0.prompt: A wildlife guide compares three birds. One is taller than all the others. Choose the correct sentence.
5-0-0.answer: It is the tallest bird of the three.
options: It is the tallest bird of the three.
It is taller bird of the three.
It is more taller than all the birds.
It is the most tall bird of three.
5-0-0.hint: A group of three needs a superlative.

5-0-1.prompt: One of two journeys takes longer. Which comparison is grammatical?
5-0-1.answer: The train journey is more tiring than the bus journey.
options: The train journey is more tiring than the bus journey.
The train journey is most tiring than the bus journey.
The train journey is tiringer than the bus journey.
The train journey is the more tiring of all three.
5-0-1.hint: Long adjectives use more + adjective + than.

5-0-2.prompt: Among four dishes, the soup tastes best. Which description is correct?
5-0-2.answer: The soup is the best of the four dishes.
options: The soup is the best of the four dishes.
The soup is better of the four dishes.
The soup is the goodest of the four dishes.
The soup is the more good dish.

5-1-0.prompt: You have visited many beaches. Which sentence identifies your favourite compared with them all?
5-1-0.answer: This is the most beautiful beach I have visited.
options: This is the most beautiful beach I have visited.
This is the more beautiful beach of all.
This beach is beautifuler than all.
This is the beautifulest of all beaches.
5-1-0.hint: Most beautiful is the superlative of a long adjective.

5-1-1.prompt: Compare only Amir and Ben. Amir runs 10 seconds; Ben runs 12 seconds. Which is true?
options: Amir is the fastest of the two than Ben.
5-1-1.hint: Lower time means faster; compare two with faster.

5-1-2.prompt: Of the three books, A has 80 pages, B has 120, C has 200. Which is correct?
5-1-2.answer: Book C is the longest of the three.
options: Book C is the longest of the three.
Book C is longer of the three.
Book A is the most long book.
Book B is longer than C.
5-1-2.hint: The greatest length among three needs longest.

5-2-0.prompt: The weather office expects heavy rain, but isn't certain. Which prediction fits?
5-2-0.answer: I think it will rain this evening.
options: I think it will rain this evening.
It rained tomorrow because of clouds.

5-2-1.prompt: A friend lost his pen. You promise to help right now. What do you say?
5-2-1.hint: Spontaneous offer uses will + base verb.

5-2-2.prompt: The science museum predicts robots in classrooms in 2050. Which statement works?
options: Robots assist will the teachers in 2050.

5-3-0.prompt: A pupil makes a promise to be on time tomorrow. Which is correct?
5-3-0.hint: Won't is will not, followed by be.

5-3-1.prompt: You want to ask politely about tomorrow's visit. Choose the correct question.
options: Do your parents will come tomorrow?
Are your parents will coming tomorrow?
5-3-1.hint: Future yes/no questions begin with Will.

5-3-2.prompt: Your team lost yesterday but expects better next week. Which sentence fits?
5-3-2.answer: We will try again next week.
options: We will try again next week.
We tried again next week yesterday.
We will trying again next week.
We are try again last week.
5-3-2.hint: Will followed by try shows future.

5-4-0.prompt: The football field is wet, ___ the match is postponed.

5-4-1.prompt: Mina is tired, ___ she continues studying.

5-5-0.prompt: Ali brought an umbrella, ___ it started raining.

5-5-1.prompt: The bus was full, ___ we waited for the next one.

5-6-0.prompt: The team thanked the volunteer. Which replacement is correct?
5-6-0.hint: After thanked, use the object pronoun.

5-6-1.prompt: "My cousins visited Aina and me." Which word replaces Aina and me?

5-7-0.prompt: The coach spoke to Danial and Amir. Replace their names correctly.
5-7-0.hint: After to, use object pronoun them.
